maths.topic: The numbers 4 and 5: find them, spot them without counting, show them
stems: "How do you see it? I see two and two."
maths.source: From the 20 November school update: finding, subitising and representing the numbers 4 and 5, and explaining how they can see the numbers. Home practice runs a week behind school for maths.
everyday: Snacks: put out four or five raisins and ask how many before they count.
How do you see it? Four grapes as two and two, or three and one. School is practising explaining this.
Dice: the four and the five faces. Where are the dots? One in each corner, and one in the middle.
Out and about: four wheels on a car, five fingers on a hand, a 4 or a 5 on a door.

steps.do: Go on a hunt: find four of something the same, then five the same (spoons, socks, cars).
Line them up and point to each group.
Your child makes a group of four or five for you to say.

stretch.label: Stretch: four, even when they are different

challenge.label: Challenge: sharing between two
challenge.say: Share them so each one gets the same.
challenge.paper: six raisins and two plates. One for you, one for me, until they are gone. How many each?

questions.say: Six apples, shared between two teddies. How many each?
questions.hint: One for you, one for me, until they are gone.

questions.say: Four apples, shared between two teddies. How many each?
questions.hint: One for you, one for me, until they are gone.

questions.say: Three and three more. How many altogether?
questions.hint: A double. Three fingers on each hand.

steps.do: Hide four or five small things under a cup. Lift it for a second, then cover again.
Your child says how many, without counting.
steps.say: How many did you see? How did you see them?

steps.do: Lift the cup and check together. Then try Quick look, at the bottom of this tab.

challenge.label: Challenge: sharing between two

questions.say: Two apples, shared between two teddies. How many each?
questions.hint: One for you, one for me.

questions.say: Four and four more. How many altogether?

steps.do: Say a number: four or five. Your child shows it on their fingers.
Swap: you show fingers, they say the number.
Show four in a different way: two on each hand, or three and one.
steps.say: Is it still four? How do you know?

questions.say: Ten sweets, shared between two children. How many each?
questions.hint: Five fingers on each hand makes ten.

questions.say: Six apples, shared between two teddies. How many each?

questions.say: Five and five more. How many altogether?

steps.do: Use a dice or dominoes: the faces with four and five dots.
Show a face for a moment. Your child says how many.
steps.say: How many dots? Where are they?

steps.do: Your child draws the four and the five on paper: one dot in each corner, then one in the middle for five.

challenge.label: Challenge: half
challenge.say: Half means two parts the same.
challenge.paper: cut a slice of toast in half: two pieces the same. Then share four strawberries: half each.

questions.hint: Share four between two. How many each?

questions.say: Two and two more. How many altogether?
questions.hint: A double. Two fingers on each hand.

steps.do: Put out three groups: three, four and five things.
Your child matches each group to the same number of claps.
Write a 4 and a 5 on paper. Number trace, at the bottom of this tab, shows how each one is formed.

lastWeek: Phonics: z, zz, qu and ch, words with an s on the end (hats, sits), and the tricky words go, no, to and into.

English: Super Milly and the Super School Day (Stephanie Clarkson), the first of two weeks. The children talked about what their own superpowers could be, that not all superheroes wear capes, and real-life superheroes.
Maths: finding the numbers 4 and 5, spotting them without counting and showing them in different ways. The children are practising explaining how they can see the numbers.
Understanding the World: maps, starting with pirate maps: looking for and naming key features. Aerial maps of the school come next. Also what makes us different and special.
school.thisWeekPhonics: sh, th, ng and nk (school hasn't said yet: these are next in Little Wandle's order)

asks.text: Superhero Day is Wednesday 25 November: children can wear a superhero costume. School asks you not to buy anything: they can make a badge or mask in school, or wear one of school's dressing-up costumes.
Keep reading books and the reading record in the book bag every day. School reads with the children three times a week and changes books on Fridays.
Look at the phonics homework sheet attached to the update (z, zz, qu, ch; go, no, to, into).
Check the Show and Tell rota outside the classrooms. This term's theme is Superheroes: something about an inspiring family member, or pictures of special people.
Add to the Daffodil competition on Arbor.
Outdoor PE times have changed: check the timetable outside the classrooms.

standing: At home: about 15 minutes of phonics and 10 of maths, including the stretch and challenge. School also taught zz last week (buzz, fizz): Monday catches it up. Friday has last week's tricky words go, no, to and into, then she, he, of and push, which are next in Little Wandle's order and not yet confirmed by school.
